note: POP and tail figures come from the flat-vol model in zenith/vault/pop.py (held to expiration, no skew, no costs) [page:concepts-vix] [repro:vrp_spx]; tiers from the strategy cards; popularity from archive titles/tags. Reliability ranks evidence first and covers only strategies with a claimed positive edge.

most_popular.name: Short strangle
most_popular.evidence_note: The edge is the index variance risk premium, which is replicated (A) [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bondarenko-2019]. It is crash-exposed, and retail 16-delta strangles net of costs, margin and tails have no independent test (C). Overall B: real but sensitive to period and implementation. Since 2009 every Cboe short-volatility index trailed the S&P 500 total return [repro:cboe_short_vol].

most_popular.name: Iron condor
most_popular.evidence_note: The condor inherits the strangle's variance-risk-premium edge but the wings are insurance that consumes most of it: tastylive's own test shows the wide condor keeps about 60% of the median profit with 38% less tail [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@03:07], and the Cboe condor index earned about cash or less since 2007 [repro:cboe_short_vol] [lit:moran-2021b]. Documented but period- and implementation-sensitive, so B; value is the capped loss and lower buying power, not extra return.

most_popular.name: 0DTE structures
most_popular.evidence_note: Edge-negative to absent after frictions: tastylive's one-year studies find a morning short-premium approach workable [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@04:03], but the peer-reviewed work finds a positive same-day variance premium that is small against spreads and tails [lit:vilkov-2023] and no feasible edge after costs: 0DTEs look expensive, not mispriced [lit:chong-todorov-2026]. Short evidence window, one market, mostly retail buyers lose, so C.

most_popular.name: Short put
most_popular.thin_evidence: No tastylive setup/management numbers or episode study specific to the naked short put in the reviewed pages; defaults come from general short-premium pages and the index put-write literature.
most_popular.model_setup: 30-delta put, 45 DTE (delta is ours; no tastylive put delta found)
most_popular.evidence_note: The edge is the index variance and put premium, replicated across independent papers (A) [lit:bondarenko-2019] [lit:carr-wu-2009]. It is a crash-exposed premium: put-writing matched the S&P 500 over 1986-2018 but has trailed it since 2007 and 2009 [repro:cboe_short_vol], and single-stock put premium is weaker and tied to informed demand [lit:xing-etal-2010]. No tastylive setup numbers or episode study exist for a naked short put in the reviewed material, so the management defaults are borrowed from the general short-premium pages.

most_popular.name: Short straddle
most_popular.thin_evidence: Only one straddle approach page, one late-day 0DTE episode study and no repro of a 45-DTE straddle; management guidance is borrowed from strangle and general-premium pages.
most_popular.evidence_note: The edge is the index variance risk premium (replicated, A) [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bondarenko-2019], and ATM straddle returns are directly documented as negative for buyers, but Broadie et al. find ATM straddle returns harder to explain than OTM puts [lit:broadie-etal-2009]. The structure itself has only one tastylive approach page and a late-day 0DTE study, with no 45-DTE straddle study or repro of our own, so the card is C: the premium is real, a retail naked straddle after costs, margin and tails is untested.

most_popular.name: Butterfly
most_popular.thin_evidence: One tastylive note, no episode study, no reproduction of the debit butterfly; only an indirect index proxy.
most_popular.evidence_note: The only evidence is one tastylive note (buy in high IV, take 25-50% of max profit, do not manage losers); there is no episode study and no reproduction of this structure. The literature on long index premium (delta-hedged long options lose on average [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003]) cuts against 'buy in high IV' as an edge, and the Cboe BFLY index proxy trailed cash and the S&P 500 since 2007 [repro:cboe_short_vol]. No edge is documented; treat it as a defined-risk payoff shape.

most_popular.name: Earnings trade (vol crush)
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive sells earnings premium for the vol crush, but its own four-stock study had high win rates with mixed to negative return on investment in a bull market and the hosts say earnings carry the smallest edge [ep:research-2024-10-21@01:45]. The literature is conditional and contradictory on whether event options are overpriced (vendor data rich, a peer-reviewed sample favors the buyer) [lit:ivolatility-2026] [lit:gao-etal-2018]. Our repro covers post-earnings drift only, not the crush trade, so the edge is C.

most_popular.name: Short call
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give mechanics only (no DTE, delta, target or loss numbers), one generic episode, no reproduction; the premium evidence is indirect and weaker on the call side.
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive has a dedicated short-call page but gives no setup, target or loss numbers, and no study of naked calls was found. The index premium is mostly on the put side: the implied-minus-realized gap on OTM calls is under half that on OTM puts [lit:hill-etal-2006], the bearish tilt fights an equity drift of 9.80% a year [lit:bondarenko-2019], and the downside of the trade is unlimited. Treat it as a directional, short-vega view with a small premium tailwind, not as a premium engine.

most_popular.name: Ratio spread
most_popular.thin_evidence: One tastylive page and one episode with a single worked example; no study, no reproduction, and the sources disagree on the profit target.
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive's page and one 2023 episode give qualitative rules and one worked example, with no study and no reproduction, and the two disagree on the profit target. The only edge is the premium on the extra short option, which is the index variance or skew premium, one crash factor [lit:kozhan-etal-2013]; exit rules reshape risk but cannot create edge [lit:williams-1991].

most_popular.name: Short call vertical (call credit spread)
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only (no DTE, delta or width rule), no episode study and no reproduction; the call-side premium evidence is indirect.
most_popular.model_setup: 30-delta short / 16-delta long call, 45 DTE (long strike is ours)
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive's pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only, and no test of call credit spreads was found. The index premium is concentrated on the put side: the implied-minus-realized gap on OTM calls is under half that on OTM puts [lit:hill-etal-2006], and the bearish tilt trades against equity drift, so the call-side edge is the thinnest part of the volatility premium. Treat it mainly as a defined-risk, short-vega expression of a view, with the volatility premium as a small tailwind.

most_popular.name: Covered call
most_popular.evidence_note: Covered calls collect a real but small volatility premium; most of the return and risk is equity beta, and since 2009 BXM trailed the S&P 500 TR on both CAGR and Sharpe [lit:israelov-nielsen-2014] [repro:cboe_short_vol]. tastylive's 45-DTE, 30-delta, high-IV setup [page:concepts-covered-call] has no episode study in the reviewed material; the index evidence (monthly ATM for BXM, 30-delta for BXMD) is the closest independent test. The benefit is lower volatility and a shallower drawdown, not extra return. The index studies are mostly Cboe-sponsored.

most_popular.name: Diagonal spread
most_popular.thin_evidence: Tastylive concept pages and one episode mention only; no episode study, no repro, and the literature does not test diagonal spreads.
most_popular.evidence_note: Tastylive-only: a concept page with explicit setup and management numbers, but no episode study or reproduction of diagonals. The structure is a mechanic (a long option financed partly by selling nearer premium; the short is only a temporary hedge). The literature on IV and term structure is indirect: it concerns sorted portfolios of single-stock options and does not test a diagonal [lit:goyal-saretto-2009] [lit:vasquez-2017]; index IV rank is not shown to be a timing edge [lit:fallon-park-2016].

most_popular.name: Short put vertical (put credit spread)
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only (no DTE, delta or width rule), and no test of put credit spreads exists; the edge is inferred from index put-write and iron-condor index evidence.
most_popular.model_setup: 30-delta short / 16-delta long put, 45 DTE (long strike is ours)
most_popular.evidence_note: The underlying edge is the index put premium (implied volatility above realized), but the long wing buys back much of it: the nearest tested structure, the iron condor with 5-delta wings, earned about 1% a year in 2007-2026 [repro:cboe_short_vol]. tastylive's pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only, and one episode claims early profit-taking adds an edge beyond the volatility premium [ep:skinny-abstract-2026-05-11@04:22], while optional-stopping theory says exit rules do not create expected profit [lit:williams-1991]. No test of put credit spreads themselves was found.

most_popular.name: Calendar spread
most_popular.thin_evidence: One tastylive concept page and one episode mention; no episode study, no repro, and the literature does not test calendar spreads.
most_popular.evidence_note: Tastylive-only: one concept page, no episode study, no reproduction. A calendar is a theta and vega structure whose payoff depends on the stock staying near the strike and on the vol of both expiries; the trade has a stated mid-40s% success rate, below a coin flip, so its edge, if any, would come from entry pricing, which no source in the bundle tests. The literature on IV timing is indirect and does not support IV rank as a timing edge for sellers [lit:fallon-park-2016] [lit:cheng-2019]; in single names a more upward-sloping IV term structure preceded higher straddle returns for buyers [lit:vasquez-2017], but no test of calendar spreads is in the bundle.

most_popular.name: Futures options (/ES, /MES, /CL, /GC, /ZB ...)
most_popular.thin_evidence: A product wrapper with no strategy-specific tastylive study or reproduction; only feature descriptions, one curve-reading episode rule, and margin/tax rule text.
most_popular.evidence_note: This is a product wrapper: tastylive pages describe features and cautions, with one episode rule about reading the futures curve [page:concepts-futures-options] [ep:math-check-2026-04-01@05:48]. Margin and tax mechanics rest on primary rule text (A) but SPAN internals and exercise style are only partly verified [lit:uscongress-irc1256-2018] [lit:cme-24-425-2024]. There is no return evidence specific to futures options, hence tier C.

most_popular.name: Iron fly / iron butterfly
most_popular.thin_evidence: One approach page, no episode study, no repro; the only numbers are a 10-50% profit-target range and a Cboe BFLY drawdown figure.
most_popular.model_setup: ATM shorts, 16-delta wings, 45 DTE (wing choice is ours)
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive-only: one approach page and a profit-target range, with no episode study or repro of an iron fly. Mechanically it is a short straddle with capped risk, so the variance-risk-premium edge is inherited from the straddle and the wings insure most of it away, as the condor evidence suggests [lit:moran-2021b]; a Cboe BFLY index drew down far more than CNDR in the one study found. C: thin and untested here.

most_popular.name: Jade lizard
most_popular.model_setup: 16-delta put + 16/5-delta call spread, 45 DTE (wing and DTE are ours; tastylive's study used 5-7 DTE)
most_popular.evidence_note: The premium sold is the index variance premium, positive on average [lit:bondarenko-2019]. tastylive's only jade lizard study reports qualitatively high win rates over a bullish sample with no figures and mid fills [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@03:47]; we have no reproduction and no independent test of this structure. The put-heavy shape adds skew exposure that is the same crash factor as the variance premium, not extra edge [lit:kozhan-etal-2013].

most_popular.name: Long vertical (debit spread)
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages and one episode rule only; no episode study, no repro and no literature test of long verticals.
most_popular.model_setup: ATM long call / 30-delta short call, 45 DTE (strikes are ours)
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive-only: payoff mechanics, a low-IV preference and a 50% profit target, with no study or repro of long verticals in the reviewed material. The literature on option returns concerns delta-hedged cross-sections, not verticals, and is no test of this card; costs decide the outcome [lit:muravyev-pearson-2020] [lit:chen-velikov-2023]. Conflict: tastylive promotes the 50% target as a sweet spot [page:concepts-vertical-spread], while the management literature says exit rules reshape the payoff but cannot create edge [lit:williams-1991].

most_popular.name: Long call
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give payoff mechanics and a low-IV preference only; no episode study, no repro and no direct long-call test in the literature.
most_popular.evidence_note: The payoff (defined loss, unlimited upside, breakeven at strike plus debit) is mechanics [page:concepts-call-options]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative on average for index options, because buyers pay the variance premium [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003]. tastylive's page advice to buy at low IV is not tested directly, and no episode study or repro covers long calls, so the card is thin.

most_popular.name: Long put
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give payoff mechanics and a low-IV preference only; no episode study or repro. The literature is on rolled index puts as hedges, not on single-name speculative puts.
most_popular.evidence_note: The payoff is mechanics (defined loss, breakeven at strike minus debit) [page:concepts-put-options]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative: continuously held index puts lose money on average, replicated across studies, while helping in sudden crashes [lit:harvey-etal-2019] [lit:bondarenko-2019]. tastylive has only a low-IV preference and no study; tier B: the cost of owning index puts is consistent across studies, but the evidence is for index hedges and tastylive adds none.

most_popular.name: Broken-wing butterfly
most_popular.thin_evidence: Two tastylive pages, no episode study, no reproduction of a broken-wing butterfly; only index proxies for the short-premium edge.
most_popular.evidence_note: Evidence is two tastylive pages (the second gives rules but no sample, win rate or study) and no episode study or reproduction of a BWB. The underlying short-premium edge is documented for the index (B overall [lit:bondarenko-2019]) but defined-risk wings gave up most of it [repro:cboe_short_vol], and a put-heavy structure is a larger bet on the same crash factor [lit:kozhan-etal-2013]. tastylive's claim of a higher chance of profit than a regular butterfly is stated without a test; treat it as a payoff shape.

most_popular.name: Poor man's covered call
most_popular.thin_evidence: One tastylive concept page; no episode study, no repro, and the literature tests only the share-based covered call.
most_popular.evidence_note: Tastylive-only: a single concept page and no episode study or reproduction of the PMCC itself. Returns come from the same small equity and volatility exposure as a covered call, which the literature measures only for the share-based version (most risk is equity beta; BXM trailed the S&P 500 since 2009) [lit:israelov-nielsen-2014] [repro:cboe_short_vol]. Long-dated deep-ITM calls add financing and extrinsic-value decay that the covered-call studies do not capture.

most_popular.name: Protective put / index put spread
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive treats the put as insurance whose premium can outweigh protection [page:concepts-hedging]; the literature and our Cboe index reproduction agree that rolled puts cost about 3 points a year and lose to simply holding less equity, while paying in fast crashes [lit:harvey-etal-2019] [lit:israelov-2018] [repro:cboe_tail_hedge]. The value is insurance with negative expected return, not an edge. Tier A applies to the cost finding, not to any return claim.

most_popular.name: VIX hedges (calls, call spreads, futures)
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give only cautions (no setup or management), and there is no episode study or direct VIX-hedge reproduction; the evidence is inferred from related volatility studies.
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive's reviewed pages only warn about cost and decay [page:concepts-vix] [page:concepts-vxx]. The literature and our spike study suggest long volatility pays a negative premium and VIX spikes mean-revert [repro:vix_spikes] [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003], but no study of VIX calls or futures as a hedge was found, so the tier is C. The value is insurance, expected-return-negative.

most_popular.name: Long straddle
most_popular.evidence_note: The payoff is mechanics: long gamma and vega, breakevens at the strike plus and minus the total debit [page:concepts-straddle]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative on average. tastylive says buy when IV is low; our test finds implied volatility above realized even at IV rank 0-20 [repro:vrp_spx], and index straddles lost about 3% a week [lit:coval-shumway-2001]. The main counterexample is pre-announcement single-stock straddles (+3.34%, 1996-2010) [lit:gao-etal-2018], and event results conflict by period and firm type, so tier C.

most_popular.name: Collar
most_popular.thin_evidence: tastylive pages carry no numbers and there is no episode study; the numbers come from an index proxy (CLL) and put-overlay research.
most_popular.model_setup: 100 shares + 30-delta call sold + 30-delta put bought (deltas are ours)
most_popular.evidence_note: tastylive's two pages describe the structure and uses but give no numbers, study or management rules. The independent evidence is that a collar is insurance, not a return source: the put leg costs about 3 points a year in index tests [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:bondarenko-2019] and protected portfolios had worse tail losses than equal-return stock/cash mixes [lit:israelov-2018]; the Cboe CLL index cut drawdown and beta but gave up a large share of the return, and a dedicated collar paper was not read [lit:israelov-klein-2016].

most_popular.name: LEAPS / deep-ITM stock replacement
most_popular.thin_evidence: Two tastylive concept pages, no episode study, no repro; the literature in the bundle does not test deep-ITM long-dated calls.
most_popular.evidence_note: The card rests on one tastylive LEAPS concept page and the ZEBRA pages, with no episode study and no reproduction of our own. The structure is a payoff mechanic (stock-like delta, premium-limited loss), not a documented source of return; the option-return literature in the bundle concerns single-stock option anomalies and does not test a long deep-ITM call. It supports only a caution that long single-stock option buyers have tended to pay for IV above realized volatility [lit:goyal-saretto-2009] [lit:cao-han-2013].

most_popular.name: Long strangle
most_popular.thin_evidence: The tastylive strangle page treats the long side briefly and no study tests long strangles; the evidence is borrowed from index straddles, delta-hedged options and our index volatility test.
most_popular.evidence_note: The payoff is mechanics: long gamma and vega, breakevens at the call strike plus and the put strike minus the total debit [page:concepts-strangle]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative on average for index options, but no study tests strangles directly, only straddles and delta-hedged options [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003]. tastylive says buy at low IV; our test finds implied volatility above realized even at IV rank 0-20 [repro:vrp_spx].

most_popular.name: Cash-secured put
most_popular.thin_evidence: One tastylive page with mechanics only (no setup numbers, no episode mentions); the edge rests on the index put-write (PUT) literature and our index reproduction.
most_popular.evidence_note: The edge is the index put premium (implied volatility above realized), documented in independent papers and in the Cboe PUT index, which is itself a cash-secured put-write [lit:ungar-moran-2009] [lit:bondarenko-2019]. It is period-sensitive: PUT matched the S&P 500 over 1986-2018 but trailed it in 2007-2026 and since 2009, with a beta near 0.60 [repro:cboe_short_vol]. The tastylive page gives only mechanics, no tested setup or management numbers, so the entry and exit defaults are general short-premium rules.

The value is insurance with negative expected return, not an edge. Tier A applies to the cost finding only.

highest_pop.model_setup: ATM long call / 30-delta short call, 45 DTE (strikes are ours)
highest_pop.evidence_note: tastylive-only: payoff mechanics, a low-IV preference and a 50% profit target, with no study or repro of long verticals in the reviewed material. The literature on option returns concerns delta-hedged cross-sections, not verticals, and is no test of this card; costs decide the outcome [lit:muravyev-pearson-2020] [lit:chen-velikov-2023]. Conflict: tastylive promotes the 50% target as a sweet spot [page:concepts-vertical-spread], while the management literature says exit rules reshape the payoff but cannot create edge [lit:williams-1991].

highest_pop.name: Butterfly
highest_pop.thin_evidence: One tastylive note, no episode study, no reproduction of the debit butterfly; only an indirect index proxy.
highest_pop.evidence_note: The only evidence is one tastylive note (buy in high IV, take 25-50% of max profit, do not manage losers); there is no episode study and no reproduction of this structure. The literature on long index premium (delta-hedged long options lose on average [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003]) cuts against 'buy in high IV' as an edge, and the Cboe BFLY index proxy trailed cash and the S&P 500 since 2007 [repro:cboe_short_vol]. No edge is documented; treat it as a defined-risk payoff shape.

highest_pop.name: Long put
highest_pop.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give payoff mechanics and a low-IV preference only; no episode study or repro. The literature is on rolled index puts as hedges, not on single-name speculative puts.
highest_pop.evidence_note: The payoff is mechanics (defined loss, breakeven at strike minus debit) [page:concepts-put-options]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative: continuously held index puts lose money on average, replicated across studies, while helping in sudden crashes [lit:harvey-etal-2019] [lit:bondarenko-2019]. tastylive has only a low-IV preference and no study; tier B: the cost of owning index puts is consistent across studies, but the evidence is for index hedges and tastylive adds none.

highest_pop.name: Long call
highest_pop.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give payoff mechanics and a low-IV preference only; no episode study, no repro and no direct long-call test in the literature.
highest_pop.evidence_note: The payoff (defined loss, unlimited upside, breakeven at strike plus debit) is mechanics [page:concepts-call-options]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative on average for index options, because buyers pay the variance premium [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003]. tastylive's page advice to buy at low IV is not tested directly, and no episode study or repro covers long calls, so the card is thin.

highest_pop.name: Long strangle
highest_pop.thin_evidence: The tastylive strangle page treats the long side briefly and no study tests long strangles; the evidence is borrowed from index straddles, delta-hedged options and our index volatility test.
highest_pop.evidence_note: The payoff is mechanics: long gamma and vega, breakevens at the call strike plus and the put strike minus the total debit [page:concepts-strangle]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative on average for index options, but no study tests strangles directly, only straddles and delta-hedged options [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003]. tastylive says buy at low IV; our test finds implied volatility above realized even at IV rank 0-20 [repro:vrp_spx].

most_reliable_defined.name: Iron condor
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: The condor inherits the strangle's variance-risk-premium edge but the wings are insurance that consumes most of it: tastylive's own test shows the wide condor keeps about 60% of the median profit with 38% less tail [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@03:07], and the Cboe condor index earned about cash or less since 2007 [repro:cboe_short_vol] [lit:moran-2021b]. Documented but period- and implementation-sensitive, so B; value is the capped loss and lower buying power, not extra return.

most_reliable_defined.name: Cash-secured put
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: One tastylive page with mechanics only (no setup numbers, no episode mentions); the edge rests on the index put-write (PUT) literature and our index reproduction.
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: The edge is the index put premium (implied volatility above realized), documented in independent papers and in the Cboe PUT index, which is itself a cash-secured put-write [lit:ungar-moran-2009] [lit:bondarenko-2019]. It is period-sensitive: PUT matched the S&P 500 over 1986-2018 but trailed it in 2007-2026 and since 2009, with a beta near 0.60 [repro:cboe_short_vol]. The tastylive page gives only mechanics, no tested setup or management numbers, so the entry and exit defaults are general short-premium rules.

most_reliable_defined.name: Butterfly
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: One tastylive note, no episode study, no reproduction of the debit butterfly; only an indirect index proxy.
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: The only evidence is one tastylive note (buy in high IV, take 25-50% of max profit, do not manage losers); there is no episode study and no reproduction of this structure. The literature on long index premium (delta-hedged long options lose on average [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003]) cuts against 'buy in high IV' as an edge, and the Cboe BFLY index proxy trailed cash and the S&P 500 since 2007 [repro:cboe_short_vol]. No edge is documented; treat it as a defined-risk payoff shape.

most_reliable_defined.name: Short call vertical (call credit spread)
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only (no DTE, delta or width rule), no episode study and no reproduction; the call-side premium evidence is indirect.
most_reliable_defined.model_setup: 30-delta short / 16-delta long call, 45 DTE (long strike is ours)
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: tastylive's pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only, and no test of call credit spreads was found. The index premium is concentrated on the put side: the implied-minus-realized gap on OTM calls is under half that on OTM puts [lit:hill-etal-2006], and the bearish tilt trades against equity drift, so the call-side edge is the thinnest part of the volatility premium. Treat it mainly as a defined-risk, short-vega expression of a view, with the volatility premium as a small tailwind.

most_reliable_defined.name: Short put vertical (put credit spread)
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only (no DTE, delta or width rule), and no test of put credit spreads exists; the edge is inferred from index put-write and iron-condor index evidence.
most_reliable_defined.model_setup: 30-delta short / 16-delta long put, 45 DTE (long strike is ours)
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: The underlying edge is the index put premium (implied volatility above realized), but the long wing buys back much of it: the nearest tested structure, the iron condor with 5-delta wings, earned about 1% a year in 2007-2026 [repro:cboe_short_vol]. tastylive's pages give mechanics and a 50% guideline only, and one episode claims early profit-taking adds an edge beyond the volatility premium [ep:skinny-abstract-2026-05-11@04:22], while optional-stopping theory says exit rules do not create expected profit [lit:williams-1991]. No test of put credit spreads themselves was found.

most_reliable_defined.name: Iron fly / iron butterfly
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: One approach page, no episode study, no repro; the only numbers are a 10-50% profit-target range and a Cboe BFLY drawdown figure.
most_reliable_defined.model_setup: ATM shorts, 16-delta wings, 45 DTE (wing choice is ours)
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: tastylive-only: one approach page and a profit-target range, with no episode study or repro of an iron fly. Mechanically it is a short straddle with capped risk, so the variance-risk-premium edge is inherited from the straddle and the wings insure most of it away, as the condor evidence suggests [lit:moran-2021b]; a Cboe BFLY index drew down far more than CNDR in the one study found. C: thin and untested here.

most_reliable_defined.name: Broken-wing butterfly
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: Two tastylive pages, no episode study, no reproduction of a broken-wing butterfly; only index proxies for the short-premium edge.
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: Evidence is two tastylive pages (the second gives rules but no sample, win rate or study) and no episode study or reproduction of a BWB. The underlying short-premium edge is documented for the index (B overall [lit:bondarenko-2019]) but defined-risk wings gave up most of it [repro:cboe_short_vol], and a put-heavy structure is a larger bet on the same crash factor [lit:kozhan-etal-2013]. tastylive's claim of a higher chance of profit than a regular butterfly is stated without a test; treat it as a payoff shape.

most_reliable_defined.name: Poor man's covered call
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: One tastylive concept page; no episode study, no repro, and the literature tests only the share-based covered call.
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: Tastylive-only: a single concept page and no episode study or reproduction of the PMCC itself. Returns come from the same small equity and volatility exposure as a covered call, which the literature measures only for the share-based version (most risk is equity beta; BXM trailed the S&P 500 since 2009) [lit:israelov-nielsen-2014] [repro:cboe_short_vol]. Long-dated deep-ITM calls add financing and extrinsic-value decay that the covered-call studies do not capture.

most_reliable_defined.name: LEAPS / deep-ITM stock replacement
most_reliable_defined.thin_evidence: Two tastylive concept pages, no episode study, no repro; the literature in the bundle does not test deep-ITM long-dated calls.
most_reliable_defined.evidence_note: The card rests on one tastylive LEAPS concept page and the ZEBRA pages, with no episode study and no reproduction of our own. The structure is a payoff mechanic (stock-like delta, premium-limited loss), not a documented source of return; the option-return literature in the bundle concerns single-stock option anomalies and does not test a long deep-ITM call. It supports only a caution that long single-stock option buyers have tended to pay for IV above realized volatility [lit:goyal-saretto-2009] [lit:cao-han-2013].

most_reliable_undefined.name: Short strangle
most_reliable_undefined.evidence_note: The edge is the index variance risk premium, which is replicated (A) [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bondarenko-2019]. It is crash-exposed, and retail 16-delta strangles net of costs, margin and tails have no independent test (C). Overall B: real but sensitive to period and implementation. Since 2009 every Cboe short-volatility index trailed the S&P 500 total return [repro:cboe_short_vol].

most_reliable_undefined.name: Covered call
most_reliable_undefined.evidence_note: Covered calls collect a real but small volatility premium; most of the return and risk is equity beta, and since 2009 BXM trailed the S&P 500 TR on both CAGR and Sharpe [lit:israelov-nielsen-2014] [repro:cboe_short_vol]. tastylive's 45-DTE, 30-delta, high-IV setup [page:concepts-covered-call] has no episode study in the reviewed material; the index evidence (monthly ATM for BXM, 30-delta for BXMD) is the closest independent test. The benefit is lower volatility and a shallower drawdown, not extra return. The index studies are mostly Cboe-sponsored.

most_reliable_undefined.name: Short put
most_reliable_undefined.thin_evidence: No tastylive setup/management numbers or episode study specific to the naked short put in the reviewed pages; defaults come from general short-premium pages and the index put-write literature.
most_reliable_undefined.model_setup: 30-delta put, 45 DTE (delta is ours; no tastylive put delta found)
most_reliable_undefined.evidence_note: The edge is the index variance and put premium, replicated across independent papers (A) [lit:bondarenko-2019] [lit:carr-wu-2009]. It is a crash-exposed premium: put-writing matched the S&P 500 over 1986-2018 but has trailed it since 2007 and 2009 [repro:cboe_short_vol], and single-stock put premium is weaker and tied to informed demand [lit:xing-etal-2010]. No tastylive setup numbers or episode study exist for a naked short put in the reviewed material, so the management defaults are borrowed from the general short-premium pages.

most_reliable_undefined.name: Jade lizard
most_reliable_undefined.model_setup: 16-delta put + 16/5-delta call spread, 45 DTE (wing and DTE are ours; tastylive's study used 5-7 DTE)
most_reliable_undefined.evidence_note: The premium sold is the index variance premium, positive on average [lit:bondarenko-2019]. tastylive's only jade lizard study reports qualitatively high win rates over a bullish sample with no figures and mid fills [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@03:47]; we have no reproduction and no independent test of this structure. The put-heavy shape adds skew exposure that is the same crash factor as the variance premium, not extra edge [lit:kozhan-etal-2013].

most_reliable_undefined.name: Short straddle
most_reliable_undefined.thin_evidence: Only one straddle approach page, one late-day 0DTE episode study and no repro of a 45-DTE straddle; management guidance is borrowed from strangle and general-premium pages.
most_reliable_undefined.evidence_note: The edge is the index variance risk premium (replicated, A) [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bondarenko-2019], and ATM straddle returns are directly documented as negative for buyers, but Broadie et al. find ATM straddle returns harder to explain than OTM puts [lit:broadie-etal-2009]. The structure itself has only one tastylive approach page and a late-day 0DTE study, with no 45-DTE straddle study or repro of our own, so the card is C: the premium is real, a retail naked straddle after costs, margin and tails is untested.

most_reliable_undefined.name: Short call
most_reliable_undefined.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give mechanics only (no DTE, delta, target or loss numbers), one generic episode, no reproduction; the premium evidence is indirect and weaker on the call side.
most_reliable_undefined.evidence_note: tastylive has a dedicated short-call page but gives no setup, target or loss numbers, and no study of naked calls was found. The index premium is mostly on the put side: the implied-minus-realized gap on OTM calls is under half that on OTM puts [lit:hill-etal-2006], the bearish tilt fights an equity drift of 9.80% a year [lit:bondarenko-2019], and the downside of the trade is unlimited. Treat it as a directional, short-vega view with a small premium tailwind, not as a premium engine.

most_reliable_undefined.name: Ratio spread
most_reliable_undefined.thin_evidence: One tastylive page and one episode with a single worked example; no study, no reproduction, and the sources disagree on the profit target.
most_reliable_undefined.evidence_note: tastylive's page and one 2023 episode give qualitative rules and one worked example, with no study and no reproduction, and the two disagree on the profit target. The only edge is the premium on the extra short option, which is the index variance or skew premium, one crash factor [lit:kozhan-etal-2013]; exit rules reshape risk but cannot create edge [lit:williams-1991].

insurance_and_long_premium.name: Protective put / index put spread
insurance_and_long_premium.evidence_note: tastylive treats the put as insurance whose premium can outweigh protection [page:concepts-hedging]; the literature and our Cboe index reproduction agree that rolled puts cost about 3 points a year and lose to simply holding less equity, while paying in fast crashes [lit:harvey-etal-2019] [lit:israelov-2018] [repro:cboe_tail_hedge]. The value is insurance with negative expected return, not an edge. Tier A applies to the cost finding, not to any return claim.

insurance_and_long_premium.name: Tail hedge (far OTM puts)
insurance_and_long_premium.evidence_note: No tastylive pages or episodes were found for this card. The cost of rolled puts is replicated (literature A) and matches our Cboe index reproduction; a positive effect on long-run growth is only an unaudited, period-specific claim (C) [lit:universa-2020]. The value is insurance with negative expected return, not an edge. Tier A applies to the cost finding only.

insurance_and_long_premium.name: Collar
insurance_and_long_premium.thin_evidence: tastylive pages carry no numbers and there is no episode study; the numbers come from an index proxy (CLL) and put-overlay research.
insurance_and_long_premium.model_setup: 100 shares + 30-delta call sold + 30-delta put bought (deltas are ours)
insurance_and_long_premium.evidence_note: tastylive's two pages describe the structure and uses but give no numbers, study or management rules. The independent evidence is that a collar is insurance, not a return source: the put leg costs about 3 points a year in index tests [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:bondarenko-2019] and protected portfolios had worse tail losses than equal-return stock/cash mixes [lit:israelov-2018]; the Cboe CLL index cut drawdown and beta but gave up a large share of the return, and a dedicated collar paper was not read [lit:israelov-klein-2016].

insurance_and_long_premium.name: Long straddle
insurance_and_long_premium.evidence_note: The payoff is mechanics: long gamma and vega, breakevens at the strike plus and minus the total debit [page:concepts-straddle]. As a source of return it is EDGE-negative on average. tastylive says buy when IV is low; our test finds implied volatility above realized even at IV rank 0-20 [repro:vrp_spx], and index straddles lost about 3% a week [lit:coval-shumway-2001]. The main counterexample is pre-announcement single-stock straddles (+3.34%, 1996-2010) [lit:gao-etal-2018], and event results conflict by period and firm type, so tier C.

insurance_and_long_premium.name: Diagonal spread
insurance_and_long_premium.thin_evidence: Tastylive concept pages and one episode mention only; no episode study, no repro, and the literature does not test diagonal spreads.
insurance_and_long_premium.evidence_note: Tastylive-only: a concept page with explicit setup and management numbers, but no episode study or reproduction of diagonals. The structure is a mechanic (a long option financed partly by selling nearer premium; the short is only a temporary hedge). The literature on IV and term structure is indirect: it concerns sorted portfolios of single-stock options and does not test a diagonal [lit:goyal-saretto-2009] [lit:vasquez-2017]; index IV rank is not shown to be a timing edge [lit:fallon-park-2016].

insurance_and_long_premium.name: Calendar spread
insurance_and_long_premium.thin_evidence: One tastylive concept page and one episode mention; no episode study, no repro, and the literature does not test calendar spreads.
insurance_and_long_premium.evidence_note: Tastylive-only: one concept page, no episode study, no reproduction. A calendar is a theta and vega structure whose payoff depends on the stock staying near the strike and on the vol of both expiries; the trade has a stated mid-40s% success rate, below a coin flip, so its edge, if any, would come from entry pricing, which no source in the bundle tests. The literature on IV timing is indirect and does not support IV rank as a timing edge for sellers [lit:fallon-park-2016] [lit:cheng-2019]; in single names a more upward-sloping IV term structure preceded higher straddle returns for buyers [lit:vasquez-2017], but no test of calendar spreads is in the bundle.

insurance_and_long_premium.thin_evidence: tastylive pages give only cautions (no setup or management), and there is no episode study or direct VIX-hedge reproduction; the evidence is inferred from related volatility studies.
